title: Security Investigation Labs
summary: Analyze synthetic captures, permissions, toy web targets, scan logs and directory graphs with Go.
description: Three phases: networking and Linux evidence; in-process web application attacks and browser-policy quizzes; infrastructure reconnaissance, privilege escalation and directory graph analysis. All inputs are fictional. Data is passed to Go functions by hidden tests; no live server or network is needed. A companion C stack-frame lab lives in Breaking and Fixing C.
outcomes: Extract evidence from varied packet captures and compute IPv4 networks and routes.
Audit archived Linux permissions and correlate root execution with writable paths.
Demonstrate injection and weak-secret forgery against toy application functions.
Correlate scan evidence and find directed privilege paths in a fictional directory graph.
